To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
two cytosolic and two plasma membrane associated phosphatidylinositide specific phospholipase D isoforms were purified and characterized from suspension cultured Catharantus roseus cells.
The 132 kD enzymes show a pH optimum of 6.5 and are dependent on the surface concentration but not on the bulk concentration.
two soluble and two membrane-bound phospholipases were purified and characterized from suspension-cultured C. roseus cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the identification and characterization of multiple isoforms of soluble and membrane bound phospholibidyl-inositol specific phosphatase D from Catharanthus Roseus suspension cultured cells, and with the elucidation of the mechanism of action of the soluble enzymes.
the characterization of the PI specific phospholipoles D from C. roseus cells, the identification of the enzyme types and the determination of the interfacial Michaeli constants of the enzymes.
the characterization of multiple forms and the kinetic properties of PI specific phospholipes D from C. roseus suspension cultured cell.
